title: Estimate 2.0: one number, and where it came from
description: The unit of quantified evidence. Every number BioSense reports is an Estimate, and estimate_type travels WITH the number rather than with the object holding it -- in one statistics row a group mean is measured while the effect between groups is derived, so an object-level label would be wrong for both. The field that keeps this honest is magnitude_estimated: when no magnitude can be computed it is false, a withheld_reason is required, and the correct output is 'direction: increase, magnitude: not yet estimated' rather than invented precision.

estimate_type.description: measured = a real instrument produced it. derived = deterministic code computed it from measured or public data. simulated = a mechanistic model produced it. predicted = a model-based forecast that is not a full simulation. target = a desired outcome a person supplied.

source_ref.description: dataset_id, analysis_id, simulator run id, knowledge_id or claim id

metric.description: A readout_id of the project where one applies

estimate_type.description: The weakest link in the chain: an effect derived from measured data is derived; a difference between two simulated values is simulated.

baseline.description: null when only a direction is known

candidate.description: null when only a direction is known

magnitude_estimated.description: false when a direction is known but no magnitude can be computed. The honest output then is 'direction predicted: increase; magnitude: not yet estimated'.

change_unit.description: 'percentage_points' when both sides are percentages, otherwise the metric's own unit

relative_withheld_reason.description: Why a percentage was not computed, e.g. a baseline too near zero for the ratio to mean anything

favourable.description: Whether the change moves the metric the way the project wants. null when the project does not say.
